input_references.role: Static vessel identity and dimensions linked by vessel_id

metadata.goal: Investigate the dynamic status of the vessel over time from its trajectory, with particular attention to changing movement dynamics.
metadata.category: single-vessel dynamic navigation status over time
metadata.header: Dynamic Vessel Status: Heading, Course, Speed, and Manoeuvring
metadata.dataset_description: This one-vessel AIS-like case retains dynamic fields available in Danish AIS: timestamp, position, SOG, COG, heading, ROT, and navigational status. It contains one continuous trajectory whose middle segment has a sustained heading–COG discrepancy, frequent course changes, slower speed, and elevated turning intensity.
metadata.source_note: Raw Danish AIS supplies the relevant field structure; this continuous trajectory supports temporal dynamic-status analysis.

insight_list.insight: The vessel develops a sustained heading–course discrepancy during the middle portion of its trajectory before gradually realigning.

plot.title: Heading–Course Discrepancy over Time
plot.description: COG and heading are plotted directly, with their absolute difference shown below across the three voyage phases.

insight_list.question: When does the vessel's heading depart from its course over ground, how large is the discrepancy, and when does it realign?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
points = pd.read_csv(dataset_path).sort_values('point_index')
def circular_gap(a, b): return abs((a - b + 180) % 360 - 180)
points['heading_cog_gap_deg'] = circular_gap(points['heading'], points['cog'])
print(points[['point_index', 'heading_cog_gap_deg']].describe())

insight_list.insight: The vessel transitions from nearly straight navigation to a middle period of intensive manoeuvring with frequent course changes, then returns to stable alignment between heading and COG later in the trajectory.

insights: The vessel develops a sustained heading–course discrepancy during the middle portion of its trajectory before gradually realigning.

The vessel transitions from nearly straight navigation to a middle period of intensive manoeuvring with frequent course changes, then returns to stable alignment between heading and COG later in the trajectory.
The vessel shifts from fast, directionally stable navigation into a slower and more manoeuvre-intensive phase, before resuming faster and steadier movement later in the trajectory.
summary: The vessel is dynamically stable at the beginning and end of the voyage, but its middle interval has a sustained heading–course offset, slower speed, and frequent turning. These signals identify one concentrated manoeuvring phase followed by a gradual return to stable transit.
